column1: # title: ENG-205 Sir Gawain Part 2 — 2 Names

column2: Gawain lies in bed while Lady Bertilak visits, counters her moves case by case, returns each day's kisses to Bertilak, yet secretly keeps the green girdle.
Lady Bertilak enters Gawain's bedroom on each of the three mornings, traps him with courtesy and love-talk, and on the third day presses the protective green girdle on him.
Bertilak rises at dawn to hunt deer, then boar, then fox, and each evening presents his kill to Gawain under the exchange-of-winnings bargain.

column1: Morgan le Faye at the castle
column2: Morgan le Faye is the ancient "crone" at Bertilak's court with whom Gawain sits in gladness between the bedroom tests, still unnamed as plotter within Fitt III itself.
The Green Chapel knight is the figure Gawain must meet at dawn on New Year's Day after the three days of hunts and temptations.
Reynard is the wily fox of the third hunt, ambushed, killed, and stripped of his pelt, which Bertilak brings home as a foul-stinking match for Gawain's three kisses.
The castle priest hears Gawain's full confession after Gawain hides the girdle and declares Gawain clean and pure enough for Doomsday.
Bertilak's huntsmen and hounds drive the deer, bay the boar, and course the fox, filling each day with the ritual noise of the chase while Gawain is tested indoors.
